differences.what: The road surface is a broken, psychedelic rainbow squiggle and static-noise pattern with large pink and white blobs. It looks like a corrupted SSR or planar-reflection shader. The reference shows dark, near-black wet asphalt with crisp white dashed center markings, solid edge lines, manhole covers and a couple of scattered paper scraps.
differences.where: Center and bottom foreground, the entire carriageway under and in front of the bridge, plus the far street at center-right
differences.fix: Replace the reflection with a stable, roughness-aware one: dark asphalt base (albedo about 0.04), roughness around 0.15-0.35 with puddle variation, and no screen-space noise or chromatic smearing. Add the white dashed center line, solid edge lines, two or three manhole covers, a drain grate along the left curb, and two or three flat paper litter decals near the bottom center.

differences.what: The pedestrian bridge is made of flat, clean, untextured lavender-grey boxes with regular panel seams. The reference bridge is heavily weathered steel or concrete: rust streaks dripping down, peeling grey-blue paint, torn posters, graffiti tags and grime, with a darker, rust-browned underside beam.
differences.where: Center, the bridge span from the stair top to the right end
differences.fix: Apply a weathered painted-metal material: desaturated blue-grey paint, orange-brown rust drips running down from the top rail and bolt lines, peeling patches, white torn poster decals and black graffiti tags on the side face, and a darker, rust-stained lower girder. Lower the overall albedo so it reads mid-dark, not pale lilac.

differences.what: The scene is lit by a flat, bright blue-purple ambient light that lifts every facade evenly, so there are no deep shadows and no warm pools of light. The reference is very dark and high-contrast. Warm tungsten and sodium light comes from the shop windows, the streetlamp, the store under the bridge and the wall lantern, against near-black cool grey surroundings.
differences.where: Whole frame, most visible on the left building facade and the far buildings
differences.fix: Cut ambient and sky fill by about 60-70% and shift it from purple to a neutral cool grey-blue. Let the warm local lights (left storefront, streetlamp, convenience store, right wall lantern, under-bridge tube) carry the exposure, and add a light exponential height fog that catches those lights.

differences.what: The left building is a flat blue-purple plane with black window holes and white blinds. The reference facade is grimy, rain-stained dark concrete with framed windows, curtains and several warmly lit interiors, and its rusty AC units have streaks running under them.
differences.where: Left half, upper floors of the near building and the building behind the bridge
differences.fix: Use a dark wet concrete material with vertical rain-stain streaks and dirt in the window recesses. Give the windows frames and mullions, light some interiors warm amber with visible curtains, and make the AC units off-white, rusty and grimy instead of clean white.

differences.what: The far end of the street is short and blocked by a dark building mass, so there is no long receding vista. The reference street runs deep into the distance: many lit windows, purple and green vertical neon signs on the right buildings, a red traffic light, a row of streetlights and atmospheric haze.
differences.fix: Extend the street corridor at least 3-4x further, with layered buildings full of lit windows, vertical purple and green neon signs on the right, a red traffic signal and a row of distant streetlamps, all fading into blue-grey fog.

differences.what: The rain streaks are too thick, too long, too sparse and too white, and they sit on top of the frame like a 2D overlay. The reference rain is fine and dense, shows mainly against light sources, and includes drips falling off the underside of the bridge.
differences.where: Whole frame, worst on the upper-left building and the left sidewalk
differences.fix: Make the streaks thinner, shorter and more numerous, at about 20-30% of the current opacity, and fade them by depth and by the background luminance behind them. Add a drip curtain from the bridge's lower edge, lit by the under-bridge tube light.

differences.what: The right-side foreground balcony is a plain dark railing in front of a flat orange-brown wall. The reference has a wet, rusty metal balcony railing, a white plastic chair at the bottom right, a cracked white pot holding a dead plant, and a wall of weathered wooden boards with diagonal X bracing above corrugated rusty metal.
differences.fix: Model the rusty balcony railing with wet specular highlights, and add the white plastic chair (bottom right corner) and the cracked white pot with dry branches. Texture the wall as rain-darkened wooden planks with X-cross battens, plus rusty corrugated sheet metal below the wall lantern.

differences.what: Street props are missing or wrong. There are no orange-and-white traffic cones at the foot of the stairs, no grey utility cabinets on the left sidewalk and no black-and-yellow bollards on the right sidewalk. The bridge's right end shows a small pink sign and a gate with yellow lights, but the reference has a red 立入禁止 sign, a yellow/black striped hazard barrier, a traffic cone and a potted plant on the bridge.
differences.where: Left sidewalk at the stair base, right sidewalk, and the right end of the bridge
differences.fix: Place 2-3 traffic cones (some tipped over) and yellow caution tape at the stair base, and two grey metal utility boxes beside them. Put black bollards with yellow bands along the right curb. On the bridge's right end add a red sign reading 立入禁止 in white, a yellow/black diagonal-striped barrier panel, an orange cone and a potted plant.

differences.what: The streetlamp on the left leans diagonally and its head is dark. The reference lamp is a straight vertical grey pole with a curved arm and a bright cool-white head that throws a visible light cone and a reflection on the street.
differences.where: Left-center, the lamp pole beside the stairs
differences.fix: Make the pole straight and vertical with a curved arm ending in an emissive LED head (about 4000K). Attach a spot light that lights the rain and puts a long specular streak on the wet road below.

differences.what: The sidewalks and the stairs are too clean and dry. The left sidewalk is large flat grey tiles, the stairs are thin dark planks, and the yellow tactile strip on the right is a clean painted stripe. The reference has small square wet paving tiles that reflect the warm storefront light, and rusty open-grate steel stairs with railings. Its right sidewalk has bright, wet, glowing yellow tactile paving and a fluorescent tube light under the bridge.
differences.where: Left sidewalk, center-left stairs, right sidewalk, and the underside of the bridge
differences.fix: Use small square tiles (about 30cm) with grout and puddle-driven roughness so they mirror the amber shop light. Make the stairs rusty steel with treads, stringers and handrails. Texture the right sidewalk as a raised yellow tactile block strip with a wet sheen. Move the emissive tube from the bridge top to the underside of the bridge, above the road.
